newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea's Kim praises loyalty of military.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea's Kim praises loyalty of military.

text.p: North Korea's state media said on Wednesday that de facto leader Kim Jong-il visited a military unit this week, the first such visit it has reported since the deaths of the minister and vice minister of defence last month.
Pyongyang's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said Kim had praised the Korea People's Army (KPA) as being "unfailingly loyal" to the country's leadership and people.

The KCNA report, monitored in Tokyo, came just hours before North Korean delegates were due to take part in a meeting with U.S. and South Korean officials in New York for preliminary discussions on four-way peace talks also involving China.
KCNA said Kim inspected military unit 212 on North Korea's west coast on Monday and praised troops for their devotion and hard work.
"He said with great satisfaction that no force on earth can match the heroic KPA, which is unfailingly loyal to the party and the leader,the country and the people," it said.
The state press has not reported a visit by Kim to an armed forces unit since one it said he made on December 31. That unit was presumed by analysts in Japan to be one from Pyongyang.
North Korea's 1.1 million-strong armed forces lost two of their top leaders last month with the death of Defence Minister Choe Kwang and First Vice Defence Minister Kim Kwang-jin.
The deaths followed the unexplained replacement of Prime Minister Kang Song-san soon after the defection to South Korea of a noted North Korean ideologue.
The ideologue, Hwang Jang-yop, is still at the South Korean mission in Beijing awaiting the conclusion of negotiations between China and South Korea.
Earlier this month, North Korea twice delayed taking part in the New York talks in what was seen as an effort to press Washington to provide more food aid to its famine-stricken people.
Last April, Washington and Seoul proposed the four-way talks to defuse tensions and eventually bring about a permanent peace to replace the 1950-1953 Korean war armistice.
North Korea had been demanding that the armistice be scrapped to pave the way for a peace treaty, but solely with the United States, something unacceptable to South Korea.
The United States fought alongside South Korea during the war, while China supported North Korea.
